_meta.indication: COPIKTRA is a kinase inhibitor indicated for adult patients with relapsed or refractory CLL or SLL after at least two prior lines of systemic therapy (current label). At original NDA approval it was also granted accelerated approval for relapsed or refractory FL after at least two prior systemic therapies.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, open-label, actively controlled trial comparing duvelisib to ofatumumab; patients randomized 1:1.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with relapsed or refractory CLL or SLL after at least one prior therapy.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Progression-free survival (PFS) per independent review committee (IRC).
pivotal_trials.result: Median PFS 13.3 months (duvelisib) vs 9.9 months (ofatumumab); HR 0.52 (95% CI: 0.39, 0.70); 1-sided log-rank p<0.0001. ORR 73% vs 45%.

pivotal_trials.design: Single-arm, open-label trial of duvelisib 25 mg twice daily in patients with FL, MZL, or SLL refractory to rituximab and chemotherapy or radioimmunotherapy; efficacy was analyzed in the FL subgroup.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with FL refractory to rituximab and to either chemotherapy or radioimmunotherapy (efficacy analyzed in 83 FL patients).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR) per IRC per 2007 revised IWG criteria.
pivotal_trials.result: In 83 FL patients, ORR per IRC 42% (95% CI: 31, 54), 1 patient (1%) CR and 34 patients (41%) PR.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=20%): diarrhea or colitis, neutropenia, rash, fatigue, pyrexia, cough, nausea, upper respiratory infection, pneumonia, musculoskeletal pain, and anemia. Serious, including fatal, infections occurred in 31% of patients; treatment-related mortality occurred in 15%.
target_moa: Duvelisib is a phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) inhibitor with dual activity against the PI3K-delta and PI3K-gamma isoforms, which play key roles in the proliferation and survival of malignant B cells.

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning for treatment-related mortality and serious toxicities: fatal/serious infections (31%), diarrhea or colitis (18%), cutaneous reactions (5%), and pneumonitis (5%); treatment-related mortality occurred in 15% of COPIKTRA-treated patients.

rems.type: A communication REMS is required to mitigate the fatal and/or serious risks of infections, diarrhea or colitis, cutaneous reactions, and pneumonitis.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application was not presented to ODAC because duvelisib is not first-in-class and did not raise new efficacy or safety issues for the recommended indications.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Overall response rate (ORR) per IRC of 42% in 83 patients with refractory FL supported accelerated approval in FL.

citations.quote: In the primary analysis of ORR per IRC in 83 patients with refractory FL, duvelisib demonstrated an ORR of 42% (95% CI: 31, 54)

confirmatory_requirement.text: A randomized phase 3 trial in relapsed or refractory FL is required as a condition of accelerated approval to confirm clinical benefit (PMR 3494-1).

citations.quote: A randomized trial is required as a condition of accelerated approval in FL in order to confirm clinical benefit.
PMR 3494-1 Conduct a randomized phase 3 clinical trial in patients with relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma that verifies and isolates the clinical benefit of duvelisib.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan drug designation granted for CLL and SLL (15 April 2013) and for FL (01 August 2013).

citations.quote: 15 April 2013	Orphan drug designation granted for treatment of CLL and SLL (13-3944)
01 August 2013	Orphan drug designation granted for treatment of FL (13-3999)

basis.text: Application received priority review; the Applicant requested priority review which the Agency granted.

citations.quote: The Applicant requested priority review, which the Agency granted.

summary.text: COPIKTRA (duvelisib) received regular approval for relapsed/refractory CLL or SLL after at least two prior therapies and accelerated approval for relapsed/refractory FL after at least two prior systemic therapies, under priority review, with orphan drug designations for CLL/SLL and FL. The FL accelerated approval required a randomized confirmatory phase 3 trial. A communication REMS and boxed warning for serious/fatal toxicities were required.

citations.quote: The benefit-risk assessment supports regular approval of duvelisib for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory CLL or SLL after at least two prior therapies and accelerated approval of duvelisib for the treatment of adult patients with refractory FL after at least two prior systemic therapies.
It is approved under the provisions of accelerated approval regulations (21 CFR 314.500)
The Applicant requested priority review, which the Agency granted.

requirement.text: PMR 3494-1: Conduct a randomized phase 3 trial in relapsed or refractory FL that verifies and isolates the clinical benefit of duvelisib, with PFS per IRC as the primary endpoint.

citations.quote: PMR 3494-1 Conduct a randomized phase 3 clinical trial in patients with relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma that verifies and isolates the clinical benefit of duvelisib. The primary endpoint would be progression-free survival as determined by an independent review committee.

requirement.text: PMR 3494-2: Characterize the safety of long-term use of duvelisib monotherapy in patients with hematologic malignancies (25 mg BID) across Trials IPI-145-02, IPI-145-06, IPI-145-07, and IPI-145-12 combined.

citations.quote: PMR 3494-2 Characterize the safety of long-term use of duvelisib monotherapy in patient with hematologic malignancies treated with a planned dose of 25 mg twice daily on Trials IPI-145-02, IPI-145-06, IPI-145-07, and IPI 145-12 combined.

requirement.text: PMC 3494-4: Conduct a clinical PK trial with repeat doses of a moderate CYP3A4 inducer on single-dose PK of duvelisib to assess decreased drug exposure and determine dosing recommendations.

citations.quote: PMC 3494-4 Conduct a clinical pharmacokinetic trial with repeat doses of a moderate CYP3A4 inducer on the single dose pharmacokinetics of duvelisib to assess the magnitude of decreased drug exposure and to determine appropriate dosing recommendations.

requirement.text: PMC 3494-5: Develop and test product characteristics of a lower strength (5 mg or 10 mg) duvelisib formulation to allow dose reduction in patients not tolerating 15 mg twice daily.

citations.quote: PMC 3494-5 To allow dose reduction of duvelisib in patients who do not tolerate 15 mg twice daily, develop and test the product characteristics of a lower strength (5 mg or 10 mg) duvelisib formulation.
